title: Grateful Dead Live at Bellarmine College on 1968-12-07

ai_review.summary: A solid ’68 soundboard capture highlighted by the ultra‑rare live “Rosemary” and a mind‑blowing late‑summer jam session.
ai_review.review: The show is praised for its subtle, high‑energy playing – especially the one‑of‑a‑kind performance of “Rosemary” and an expansive Dark Star/Stephen/“11‑Jam”/Death Don’t sequence. The soundboard recording is considered good for its era, though a few reviewers note occasional sound problems and missing portions.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high marks (4‑5 stars) emphasize exceptional musical performance and a decent, historically respectable recording; minor technical hiccups keep the rating just below top‑tier.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally clear for a 1968 board tape – “pretty good for ’68” – but some reviewers mention occasional sound problems, missing sections and modest audience bleed.

standout_songs: Dark Star > Stephen > 11 Jam > Death Don't
show_quality.setlist_flow: A mellow, low‑pressure first half that builds into a loose, exploratory second set with extended jams; early sound hiccups give way to freer playing as the night progresses.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Blistering Garcia guitar licks are clearly audible and praised throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil’s bass is heard occasionally, adding depth to the jam sections.
band_member_comments.Keys: Organ/keyboard parts surface faintly at times, noted but not dominant.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drummers are audible, providing a solid backbone for the laid‑back vibe.
